message.content:
Below is a quick “recipe” you can copy‑paste into your terminal or script.  
It shows exactly what URL to hit, how to authenticate, and how to pull out **only** the `id` fields of the CNAME records.

---

### 1️⃣ Make the HTTP request  

```bash
curl -sS \\
    -H "x-apikey: secret123" \\
    "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records"
```

> *Explanation*  
> • `-sS`: silent mode but still prints errors.  
> • Header `x-apikey` carries your API key (`secret123`).  
> • Endpoint `/api/v3/domains/<DOMAIN>/dns_records` lists all DNS records for the given domain.

---

### 2️⃣ Extract the CNAME record IDs  

#### Using jq (command line)

```bash
curl -sS \
    -H "x-apikey: secret123" \
    "https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records" |
jq '[.data[] | select(.attributes.record_type==\"CNAME\") | .id]'
```

Result (example):

```json
[
  "d5f8e9b7a0c12ab34cd567890efghijk",
  "a1b2c3d4e5f67890123456789abcdefg"
]
```

#### Or in plain Python

```python
import requests

API_KEY   = "secret123"
BASE_URL  = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3"

headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}
resp    = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/domains/sample.com/dns_records", headers=headers)
resp.raise_for_status()

ids = [item["id"]
       for item in resp.json()["data"]
       if item["attributes"]["record_type"].upper() == "CNAME"]

print(ids)          # e.g., ['d5f8e9...', 'a1b2c3...']
```

---

### What you’ll see

A single JSON array containing **just the identifiers** of every CNAME entry found on `sample.com`. No other metadata—exactly what you asked for.
